- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) or shows strong reversal, model often fails to adjust downward; apply downward bias of 2–5% if sentiment drops below 0.33.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model frequently overcorrects or overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above peak or use 3-period moving average for smoothing.  
- Model underestimates mean reversion in downward trends; if 3–5 consecutive days show falling prices, add 1–2% downward bias to next forecast.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overpredicts early in the window; apply 1–3% downward adjustment for first 5–7 days if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.  
- If sentiment history includes a recent negative event (e.g., -1.00), model tends to ignore it; adjust forecast downward by 2–4% if sentiment was negative in last 3–5 days.
